sections.preamble: You answer questions about a single medical image. Follow the answer format requested in the user message exactly.

content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a soft-tissue mass.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The image shows a thigh cross-section. The bright heterogeneous mass lies on the image left, near the femur region, at roughly x=250-370, y=300-540 in the left panel. In the right panel this corresponds to x≈1030-1150.

Mark 660 sits at (1042, 380), which falls on the bright heterogeneous tissue at the left edge of the mass. Mark 650 at (1121, 350) is close to the bright elongated structure at the upper part of the mass (left panel x≈337, y≈350). Mark 647 at (1097, 411) lies in the dark region between structures, which is probably bone or a flow void.

The left panel shows the bright elongated structure at about x=310-360, y=310-380, which maps to x≈1094-1144 in the right panel. Mark 650 at (1121, 350) falls within it. Mark 660 at left-panel x=258, y=380 lies in the lumpy bright tissue, which is also part of the mass.

The mass seems to extend from the upper bright part (x≈330, y≈320) down to the lower bright area (x≈280, y≈500). Its centre is around x≈290, y≈420, which maps to right-panel x≈1074, y≈420. The nearest marks are 647 (1097, 411), 645 (1048, 448) and 660 (1042, 380).

Mark 660 is at the left edge of the lumpy bright tissue and is the one clearly inside the mass. It is the highlighted mark, and it sits in tissue that is bright and heterogeneous.

ANSWER: 660
